title: Metrics, dashboards and traces
goal: See the system. Prometheus scrapes the gateways, the worker and llama.cpp; Grafana opens on a provisioned dashboard with TTFT, TPOT, tokens/s, queue depth, cache hit rate and shed rate; OpenTelemetry traces flow from nginx through the gateway and router to the replica call, and through NATS to the worker, in Jaeger.

changes.note: prom-client registry: RED counters and histograms, TTFT/TPOT histograms, tokens, shedding, cache results; gauges read at scrape time.
OpenTelemetry NodeSDK: http, undici (fetch), pg and ioredis instrumentation, OTLP/HTTP to Jaeger.
router.route_and_admit and llm.generate spans; metrics at every outcome.
Injects traceparent into NATS message headers.
Extracts it and continues the trace; worker metrics on :9100.
/metrics; route-template labels; queue, in-flight and batch gauges.
ngx_otel_module: nginx spans, traceparent propagation, trace id in the access log.
Scrape gateways, worker, llama.cpp replicas every 5 s.
SLO alerts: TTFT p95, TPOT p95, shed rate, 5xx ratio.
Prometheus and Jaeger data sources with fixed uids.
Latency, RED, saturation (USE), caches and batch.
prometheus, grafana, jaeger; nginx switches to the -otel image.

verify.label: Prometheus targets are up
verify.cmd: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/targets | python3 -c "import sys,json;[print(t['labels']['job'],t['labels']['instance'],t['health']) for t in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['activeTargets']]"
verify.expect: gateway-a, gateway-b, worker, llm-1..3 and prometheus, all 'up'.

verify.label: Gateway metrics
verify.expect: llm_ttft_seconds_count{replica=...,tier="gold"} with counts, gateway_queue_depth per replica, llm_tokens_total by type and tier.

verify.label: llama.cpp's own metrics
verify.cmd: docker compose exec llm-1 curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep -E '^llamacpp:' | head
verify.expect: Lines such as llamacpp:prompt_tokens_total, llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total, llamacpp:requests_processing (exact names depend on the llama.cpp build).

verify.label: The dashboard
verify.expect: Grafana (no login needed to view) shows 'LLM platform (capstone)' with TTFT, TPOT, tokens/s, queue depth, cache hit ratio and shed rate filling in.

verify.label: One trace across nginx, gateway, router and replica
verify.cmd: curl -s -D - -o /dev/null localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}' && docker compose logs nginx | tail -1
verify.expect: The nginx log line ends with trace=<32 hex characters>. Search that id in Jaeger (http://localhost:16686): nginx -> llm-gateway POST -> router.route_and_admit and llm.generate -> POST to llm-N (undici), plus redis and pg spans.

verify.label: Alerts are loaded
verify.expect: TTFTp95High, TPOTp95High, HighShedRate, ServerErrorRatio (and the group name).

concepts.how: RED for the API, USE for replicas (in flight, queue depth), histograms for percentiles, low-cardinality labels only.
W3C traceparent propagated through nginx, fetch and, by hand, through NATS message headers.
Structured JSON logs carrying request ids; nginx logs the trace id so a log line leads to its trace.
TTFT p95 and TPOT p95 as SLIs with targets; shedding counted separately from failures.
Alert on symptoms users feel (latency, errors), with a 'for' duration to avoid flapping.
The LLM-specific signals: TTFT, TPOT, tokens/s per user versus aggregate.

checkpoints.text: All Prometheus targets are up and the Grafana dashboard shows TTFT, TPOT and tokens/s.
I followed one trace id from the nginx log to Jaeger and saw nginx, gateway, router and replica spans.
I found a batch job's trace continuing from POST /v1/batches into the worker.
I can explain why tenant ids are not metric labels.
